statements.text: I think the thing that scares me the most is that we are going to have a system where we are going to have AI-generated letters which we receive from constituents that are then going to be AI-generated letters back to those AI- generated—it is just going to be this vicious circle.
statements.context: Remarks at a House hearing on AI innovations within the legislative branch.

statements.text: I do want to go to what Ms. Sewell said [...] about the AI logarithms and how we can do things to avoid any type of unintended consequences, if you will. [...] Briefly, if you could, how does the CAO regulate, collect, and inventory AI use cases?
statements.context: House hearing on AI innovations within the legislative branch, where Rep. Carey asks the Chief Administrative Officer about internal AI governance.

statements.text: CRS' modernization initiatives as it relates to AI, can you tell us more about the working group and particularly the work in exploring how AI might be used to expedite bill summary process?
statements.context: Legislative hearing on modernizing the Congressional Research Service and federal data use.

statements.text: And AI is going to do a lot of functions extremely well and create tremendous benefits, but it has to be overseen or basically spell-checked or whatever you want to say so things like this don't happen.
statements.context: Spoken at a CFTC oversight hearing examining commodity markets and AI integration.

statements.text: In this regard, Chairwoman Bice and I are constantly looking to understand how other Government offices are incorporating AI and machine learning systems into their daily operations.
statements.context: House Oversight Committee hearing on the Government Publishing Office in a digital-first era, where a member asks about AI tools and an open data protocol.
